root.label: Callable wrappers
root.note: Type-erased holders for callables, plus the invoke rules and binders beneath them.

children.label: std::function
children.note: The C++11 copyable wrapper that keeps only the call signature.

children.label: Copyable target
children.note: The stored callable must be copy constructible, so move-only closures are rejected.

children.label: Empty call
children.note: Calling an empty function throws bad_function_call.

children.label: Const hole
children.note: operator() is const but calls the target non-const, so a mutable lambda mutates.

children.label: Small buffer
children.note: Only encouraged by the standard; large targets may allocate, and the limit varies by library.

children.label: Qualified signatures
children.note: Newer wrappers put const, reference and noexcept qualifiers in the signature.

children.label: move_only_function
children.note: C++23 owning wrapper that is move only and accepts move-only targets.

children.label: copyable_function
children.note: C++26 copyable counterpart with the same qualifier support.

children.label: Empty call is UB
children.note: Unlike function, calling an empty one of these is undefined behavior.

children.label: Const-correct
children.note: A const in the signature rejects a mutable target at construction.

children.label: function_ref
children.note: C++26 non-owning view of a callable.

children.label: No allocation
children.note: It stores a reference and a thunk, is trivially copyable, and never allocates.

children.label: Dangling risk
children.note: Calling it after the target is destroyed is undefined behavior, as with string_view.

children.label: invoke rules
children.note: INVOKE is the single definition of calling, used throughout the library.

children.label: Member pointers
children.note: The first argument may be an object, reference, pointer, smart pointer or reference_wrapper.

children.label: Value category
children.note: A data member pointer yields a result whose category follows the object.

children.label: Binders
children.note: Ways to fix some arguments of a callable.

children.label: bind
children.note: Stores decayed copies, uses placeholders, and drops extra call arguments.

children.label: bind_front and bind_back
children.note: Bind leading or trailing arguments with perfect forwarding and no placeholders.

children.label: Lambdas
children.note: Usually clearer and more optimizable than any binder.

children.label: Helpers and cost
children.note: Small adapters, and what the wrappers cost.

children.label: reference_wrapper
children.note: A copyable reference that rebinds on assignment; made by ref and cref.

children.label: mem_fn and not_fn
children.note: mem_fn adapts member pointers; not_fn negates a callable's result.

children.label: Cost model
children.note: An indirect call that rarely inlines, plus a possible allocation on construction.
